answer: Peer-Cohort Cost Splitting. Each agent identity must be sponsored by 3 existing agents who jointly absorb a share of any loss caused by that identity, with the sponsor liability rising against a rotating tide of recent adverse events. Sponsors also forfeit a small ivory-token deposit when a sponsored identity is later flagged, and their own reputation drops. A raven flag marks clusters of linked sponsors for audit. Cloning now requires recruiting independent sponsors willing to risk real holdings, so each marginal clone costs more than its expected gain.
